headline: Commercial nuclear surge lifts BWXT · guidance raised
summary_short: BWXT reported Q2 2026 revenue of $901.6M (+18% y/y) with Commercial Operations up 72% on nuclear power demand. Non-GAAP EPS of $1.07 rose from $1.02 a year ago. Company raised FY2026 EBITDA, EPS, and free cash flow guidance.
summary_long: Revenue rose 18% y/y to $901.6M, led by a 72% jump in Commercial Operations to $302.5M on commercial nuclear components, field services, fuel handling, medical, and the Kinectrics contribution. Government Operations grew 2% to $601.3M on naval propulsion and special materials, offset by lower advanced nuclear volumes. GAAP EPS was $0.97 (non-GAAP $1.07). Adjusted EBITDA of $155.5M rose 7%. BWXT announced the sale of its medical business to sharpen focus on core nuclear defense and commercial power, and closed the Precision Components Group (PCG) acquisition July 1 to build U.S. commercial nuclear manufacturing footprint. Backlog reached $8.40B, up from $6.02B a year ago. FY2026 guidance raised across all key metrics.

drivers.explanation: Commercial Operations growth of 72% led by commercial nuclear components, field services, fuel handling, medical, and Kinectrics contribution; Government Operations up 2% on naval propulsion and special materials, offset by lower advanced nuclear volumes.

Higher non-GAAP operating income from Commercial Operations growth partially offset by higher corporate expense and lower Government Operations from unfavorable mix and prior-year positive contract adjustments.
Higher operating income and lower interest expense partially offset by lower other income and a higher tax rate.
Higher net income, an increase in advanced billings, and good working capital management were offset by timing of income tax payments.
